scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You see someone yawn, and suddenly you're yawning too. Why do we yawn at all? Science is still not fully sure.

scenes.name: what
scenes.text: A yawn is a long, deep breath in with the jaw wide open, followed by a quick breath out.

scenes.name: oxygen
scenes.text: People thought yawning brings in oxygen, but studies found breathing extra oxygen doesn't reduce yawning.

scenes.name: cool
scenes.text: A leading idea is that yawning helps cool the brain, by drawing in air and increasing blood flow.

scenes.name: alert
scenes.text: We yawn more when tired or bored, so it may help the brain shift states and stay alert.

scenes.name: contagious
scenes.text: Yawns are contagious, especially between friends and family, possibly linked to social bonding and empathy.

scenes.name: animals
scenes.text: Many animals yawn too, including dogs, cats and fish, so it's a very old behaviour.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Deep breath, brain cooling, contagious. Still a bit of a mystery. Follow for more on how things really work.
